operations: Built-in targeted edit: add a Napoleonic bicorne to local theodolite master
Copy edited PNG unchanged into revision_v3
Add transparent canvas margins and center visible group mechanically; original edited RGBA pixels exactly preserved
Downscale and contact sheets only; no painting, masking or recoloring

entries.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE original TECHNOLOGY invention icon for Victoria 3 / 1776 Age of Revolutions.
Style/medium: native-compatible hand-painted volumetric illustration, broad readable forms, restrained matte fine grain, soft upper-left light and slightly darker undersides. Natural individually colored materials; not a flat PM pictogram, glossy CGI, photograph, gold badge or uniform sepia.
Composition: one compact coherent conceptual group, isolated with generous transparent margins, entire useful silhouette visible. Square high-resolution image at least 1024 pixels, legible at 48/64 pixels. No framed building vignette or separately displayed foreground commodity.
Background: genuine transparent alpha outside the subject and through gaps; no fake black, white or checkerboard background, room, floor, landscape, sky, frame, medallion, plinth or external cast shadow.
Constraints: no text, numerals, logos, watermark, modern plastic, red-cross emblem, electronics, modern rubber tires or global blue/teal cast. Materials are warm brown wood/leather, neutral dark iron, pale linen and restrained brass. References inform the broad period and function, not an exact artifact reconstruction. Return ONE icon, never a sheet.
Primary subject:
ONE COMPACT PORTABLE VETERINARY MEDICINE KIT for military horses, early nineteenth-century conceptual equipment. A small open dark-brown wooden fitted chest with modest brass hinges contains three simple cork-stoppered amber-glass medicine bottles, a neatly rolled nearly-white linen bandage and a plain small steel instrument, all resting in coherent internal compartments. The hinged lid is open, plain and unlabelled. ONE large worn dark-iron HORSESHOE leans upright against the near side of the chest, prominently readable and attached visually to this single group, signifying equine care. Keep the kit dominant, the horseshoe clearly subordinate but identifiable, readable care supplies rather than a treasure chest. Natural warm wood and off-white cloth, modest glass highlights, no decorative carving or modern bag. NO blood, injury, exposed organs, red cross, medical symbols, labels, papers, scattered medicine, shiny crystals or separate background horse. This is an interpretation of regimental veterinary care, not an exact named military kit.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: one transparent TECHNOLOGY invention icon for Victoria 3 / 1776 Age of Revolutions, Corps du génie.
Input image 1: EDIT TARGET, the existing brass theodolite on its short three-legged oak tripod.
Primary request: add exactly ONE Napoleonic-era officer's BICORNE HAT as the single meaningful supporting accessory. The black wool felt bicorne has two clearly shaped upturned wings, restrained broad antique-gold edge braid with subtly woven oak-leaf texture, one small round blue-center/red-middle/white-outer tricolor cockade held by a gold loop and plain gold button. Inspired by the ceremonial headwear attributed to engineering officer General Bertrand in the Musée du Génie catalog, not a certified reproduction or an exclusive engineer-regimental issue. NO plume, feathers, tall shako, modern cap, helmet, fantasy badge, engineer symbol or eagle.
Placement: a compact bicorne rests naturally beside the tripod's lower feet, below the surveying instrument, slightly in the foreground. It forms one coherent group with the instrument rather than floating. Keep the hat clearly subordinate, roughly one-third of the overall group width; show enough of both upturned wings and cockade to identify it at 48/64 pixels. Do not cover the telescope, graduated circle, compass, central mounting or tripod head; retain a readable three-legged tripod. Use the existing transparent lower-corner space as much as possible.
Invariants: preserve the existing theodolite's straight telescope, one horizontal brass circle, vertical angle arc, compass, coherent mounts and exactly THREE oak legs. Preserve its orientation, shape, warm natural wood/brass colors, fine matte texture, soft upper-left illumination and painted volumetric native-compatible style. No reconstruction of the device, no new tools, maps, paper, soldier, gabion, table, floor, ground patch, frame or medallion. Do not introduce text, letters, numerals, watermark or logo. Do not make a uniform gold or blue icon.
Background: genuine transparent alpha outside the entire group and through open instrument/tripod gaps. Preserve existing transparency; no fake black, white or checkerboard backdrop and no external ground shadow.
Output: ONE square high-resolution edited icon at least 1024 pixels, the complete hat and instrument silhouette inside the canvas with generous margins. Only the hat addition is requested.

Primary subject:
A COMPACT EARLY NINETEENTH-CENTURY HORSE-ARTILLERY TRANSPORT GROUP, in elevated three-quarter view along a diagonal so the silhouette fills a square. Exactly TWO healthy chestnut/bay horses stand side by side at the front in plain period brown-leather draught harness, with anatomically coherent four legs each, natural hooves, heads, tails and no rider. They are connected by taut coherent traces to ONE small wooden two-wheeled artillery LIMBER carrying a modest plain closed ammunition chest. The limber is attached by a visible functional pintle hitch to the tail end of ONE lightweight muzzle-loading FIELD CANNON carriage behind it. The cannon has its own ONE axle and TWO large wooden spoked iron-rimmed wheels, a connected wooden trail, and ONE continuous straight restrained bronze barrel held on trunnions; the barrel points away from the horses, backward along the same travel axis. FOUR vehicle wheels total: two limber wheels and two gun wheels, coherent axles rather than floating extra wheels. Use weathered warm wood, muted bronze, dark iron and warm brown horses. Clearly distinguish the horse team, limber and light gun as one connected apparatus. For icon-scale this is a deliberately reduced symbolic pair, NOT a claim that two horses were a full standard gun team. NO soldiers, battlefield, soil, road, grass base, flags, plume, uniforms, ornate carving, modern recoil system, gun shield, rubber tire, red cross, logos or writing. No disconnected cannon, loose horse heads, bent tube or pointy ornamental wheel hubs.
